methods.what: Dirichlet-type integral of the deviation from the Cauchy–Riemann equations, required to be finite for a function with prescribed singularities and boundary values
Prescription of singular behaviour: near each discontinuity point a_k the function behaves like a given function ξ_k(z)

items.english: The integral ... dS must take a finite value if β is determined so that α+βi in the neighbourhood of the first discontinuity point equals ξ_1.

items.english: If α+βi is a function of x, y which near the first discontinuity point equals ξ_1 z, has a given value at the boundary, and has (continuous) difference quotients, then the integral extended over the whole surface S must have a finite value.
